claims.paper: src/config.js:300 (FRY.DETECT_L: 'larvae this small are seen 0.2 → 1 … Margulies 1989')
claims.claim: Margulies 1989 supports small larvae (< 6-15 mm) being seen less by predators
claims.note: Margulies 1989 has no predation or detection experiment. Its only remark on predation is that 'predation by planktivorous fishes on yolk-sac larvae is probably substantial', citing laboratory experiments in Margulies 1986 (the thesis), p. 69 (PDF p. 7). The size-dependent predation the paper reports in §3.6.5 is Margulies 1990 (abstract) - and as §3.6.5 words it (bluegill killed nearly every larva under 6 mm), it points the other way from 'small larvae are seen less'. Drop the 1989 citation from DETECT_L or replace it with the right source.

notes: Full text (10 pp.) read: methods, results, Tables 1-3 and Figs. 1-6 on the page images, discussion. Two small paper corrections (Table 3.6-1 egg diameter 0.87-0.92 mm, preserved eggs; Table 3.6-6 'food in excess' should be '800 rotifers/L, well fed, first 8 days') and one code citation to fix (config.js:300 DETECT_L cites Margulies 1989 for detection; the paper has nothing on it). Everything else - the egg and yolk-sac equations, hatch sizes, first-feeding size and mass, the hatch percentages, the feeding-delay and low-food survival losses, the 50-800/L bracket - checks. Conditions worth stating in the rewrite: Chesapeake (Potomac/Patuxent) stock, 1 ‰ salinity, the marine rotifer Brachionus plicatilis as food, constant 200-300 lux, 13:11 light:dark; hatch percentages are rough estimates from dead-egg removals. Other values available: hatchling dry mass ~35 µg; first feeders had used ≥ 98 % of yolk and 55-75 % of oil; optimum for development and growth 15-20 °C, hatch optimal at ≤ 17 °C; a 4 °C drop could prolong the yolk-sac stage by ≥ 3 days; white perch spawn at 10-20 °C in Chesapeake tributaries (Hardy 1978, as cited). The 'follow-on mention' in §3.6.5 line 633 is Margulies 1990 (a different work), not this paper.
